kind: borrowed object lifetime and attempt recovery closure

failureDistinction.statement: R3-WR reproduced the CLASS (a borrowed object store that cannot deliver an object makes a worker unable to commit) and never identified the ORIGIN of the original trigger; R3-WR2 preserves that distinction rather than collapsing it
failureDistinction.implication: the readiness gate is justified by the reproduced class; no claim is made about the historical origin

CREATE_TIME_READINESS.question: was the world commit-capable at the moment it was handed over

ATTEMPT_LIFETIME_VALIDITY.question: does the world stay usable for the whole attempt

validityScopes.relation: create-time readiness does NOT imply lifetime validity; the borrowed store can become unreadable after the check returns, which the lifetime matrix measures

readinessCriterion.shape: ALLOWLIST of positive exit-code facts, not a denylist of error strings
readinessCriterion.why: a denylist cannot bound the failures it does not know about, so an unseen failure falls through to READY

facts.establishes: the world names a commit, not merely a ref
the borrowed store can deliver the basis
the index and work tree are readable
git reports it would commit, or nothing to commit

failuresTheOldDenylistMissed.signature: fatal: .git/index: index file smaller than expected
fatal: Unable to create '...index.lock': File exists

exitOneRule.whySafe: measured: `commit --dry-run` does NOT run the pre-commit hook, so a hook refusal cannot masquerade as exit 1
exitOneRule.whyNotStatusText: requiring a clean tracked status would refuse a world whose worker has made UNSTAGED edits, which is exactly the state a resumed attempt is in

readinessCriterion.limit: a pre-commit hook refusal is not detected, because `--dry-run` does not run the hook; this is a property of git, not a gap in the criterion

idempotencyContract.declaredContract: the same world id reuses the path
idempotencyContract.whyLoadBearing: when an invocation throws after dispatch, Ordarium leaves the operation UNCERTAIN and the idempotent recovery path is redispatch-same-key, which re-runs this action with the same world id — so the contract IS the convergence condition of the recovery engine
idempotencyContract.defect: GitCliPort.createWorld ran `git clone` unconditionally, so a second call failed with "destination path already exists and is not an empty directory" and the redispatch could never converge
idempotencyContract.observedConsequence: Gate F FAIL_AFTER_CLONE: the retry was refused, the attempt stayed at CREATED, and the project could not advance
idempotencyContract.repair: the world is REUSED when it already exists — the clone is skipped and the basis checkout and identity are re-applied
idempotencyContract.whyReuseAndNotReClone: a world that exists may hold a worker uncommitted work; `checkout --detach` at the SAME commit preserves it (measured), while deleting and re-cloning would destroy it

workerTokenFinding.HOST_GIT_OBJECT_ACCESS: borrowed objects readable, HEAD and basis resolvable, commit capable
workerTokenFinding.WORKER_GIT_OBJECT_ACCESS: borrowed objects readable under the shipped Low-integrity write-restricted token, HEAD and basis resolvable, commit performed
workerTokenFinding.confinementControl: a Medium + NO_READ_UP canary OUTSIDE the world was DENIED to the worker (EPERM) while the world content was readable, so the confinement was in effect and the parity was not measured through an unconfined process
workerTokenFinding.confidentialityPreserved: no label was removed, no read granted and no profile relaxed to obtain the result
workerTokenFinding.measuredArtefact: the write-restricted token cannot create an anonymous pipe, so a piped-stdio git invocation fails with EPERM for reasons unrelated to object access; the shipped runner uses inherited stdio, and this measurement redirects git output to files inside the world

topologies.built: the R3-L0C rig, by copying a prepared world and cloning from the copy

survives.why: the pointer still names the original, and the copy is simply unused
repacking rewrites the store in place, so the pointer stays valid

survives.fault: borrowed store temporarily unavailable, then restored
survives.why: the world is unchanged by the outage and commits again once the store returns

breaks.mechanism: the objects the world needs are gone; commit fails with the worker signature `fatal: could not parse HEAD`

breaks.fault: borrowed store temporarily unavailable at commit time
breaks.mechanism: the same signature, and the failure is RECOVERABLE once the store returns
the alternates pointer is ABSOLUTE, so relocating the parent leaves a path that no longer resolves — the borrow is pinned, not relocatable

breaks.fault: failure after edits but before commit
breaks.mechanism: the edits remain in the worktree and uncommitted; the world is recoverable once the store returns, but nothing was committed

borrowLifetimeMatrix.lifetimeProperty: the world usable lifetime is bounded by the lifetime of a directory it does not own, and by that directory staying at its recorded ABSOLUTE path

alternatives.idea: keep the borrowed store alive for as long as a world that borrows it exists
alternatives.tradeoff: requires an owner-side registry and a release path; adds lifecycle state to a directory that currently has none

alternatives.idea: copy the borrowed objects into the world so it owns them
alternatives.tradeoff: removes the dependency entirely at the cost of duplicating history per world — the cost `--shared` exists to avoid, and it would be paid on every attempt

alternatives.idea: record the pointer relative to the world so a moved parent follows
alternatives.tradeoff: only helps when the parent moves WITH the world; a parent moved independently still breaks, and the pointer would then be wrong in a new way

continuationFinding.correctedStatement: a failed or terminated worker DOES have a supported continuation: the SAME attempt is resumed, its retained work is preserved, and it settles

arms.workerOutcome: the worker threw, so no outcome was ever returned
the borrowed store destroyed for good, so a resumed worker still cannot commit

continuationFinding.whyLegitimate: the resume goes through the SAME supported controller path (`start` → admission RESUME → the existing position), the SAME attempt id, and the SAME world; no verification is skipped, no promotion is forced and quiescence is not disabled
continuationFinding.residualGap: an attempt whose world can NEVER be committed in has no authorized terminal path: the controller exposes no abandon/cancel/terminalize operation, so the attempt stays RUNNING and the project cannot take its next structural revision
continuationFinding.residualIsNot: a defect in the resume path — it is the absence of a terminal path for a permanently impossible attempt
continuationFinding.canonicalChangeRequired: a terminal path for a permanently-uncommittable attempt would require new canonical semantics (an abandon/terminal event with its own authorization), which this stage reports rather than invents

preparationFailureFinding.partialWorldNeverPresented: measured: in both arms the worker never ran, so no partially created world was handed over as READY
preparationFailureFinding.idempotencyPreserved: measured: the retry reuses the SAME attempt id and mints no duplicate, which is what the pre-repair FAIL_AFTER_CLONE arm VIOLATED before the idempotency fix
preparationFailureFinding.uncommittedDataPreserved: the partial world is reused, not deleted, so a world that held work would keep it

unitKnownFailure.test: test/r3l0c_containment.test.ts > §10 the DECLARED layout blocks the sibling world, by traversal and by absolute path
unitKnownFailure.proof: the same test fails IDENTICALLY at the baseline commit 65fdbb1908348cf58a5e800f61795fc99c0c280b in a clean worktree, before any R3-WR2 change, deterministically across three consecutive runs
unitKnownFailure.cause: host-dependent ACL/fence behaviour in the R3-L0C containment suite; it imports neither src/effects/git_port.ts nor any file R3-WR2 changed

regression.architecture: PASS, 0 violations, 9 accepted baseline exceptions observed
regression.historicalEvidenceImmutability: PASS (325 protected files, 0 changed / 0 added / 0 removed)

residuals: the ORIGIN of the historical object-store trigger remains unidentified; only the CLASS is reproduced

an attempt whose world can never be committed in has no authorized terminal path: the controller exposes no abandon/cancel/terminalize operation, so the attempt stays RUNNING and the project cannot take its next structural revision. Closing it needs new canonical semantics, which were NOT invented
the readiness gate does not detect a pre-commit hook refusal, because git --dry-run does not run the hook — a property of git, stated rather than hidden
a borrowed world cannot survive its parent being MOVED, because the alternates pointer is absolute

environmentIncident.what: this session ran `pnpm add -D @playwright/test` to restore an e2e toolchain whose package directory was empty in this worktree. The command emptied 164 of 248 package directories in the pnpm virtual store.
environmentIncident.howDiscovered: the subsequent `npx vitest` / `npx tsc` invocations failed with MODULE_NOT_FOUND, and a directory count showed 164 empty package dirs
environmentIncident.repair: removed node_modules and reinstalled OFFLINE from the intact pnpm content-addressable store; the store was verified populated first, so the reinstall restored the exact pinned versions rather than fetching anything new
environmentIncident.verifiedAfterRepair: tsc 7.0.2, vitest 4.1.10 and playwright 1.63.0 all resolve; build clean; the full unit suite and the e2e suite were then run to completion on the repaired tree
environmentIncident.effectOnEvidence: none — the repair restored the same pinned versions and the affected measurements were re-run afterwards
